output.reply:
I recommend Route 1 for the fixture because it preserves the supplied visual direction. Both proposals use one HTML file with embedded CSS and JavaScript, native buttons, and no external assets or libraries. Native buttons support keyboard activation. Browser/version, available time, and measured effort remain unknown.

The main functional risk is incorrect or duplicate activation. The shared test below checks that risk; no test has been run. Fixture records do not establish actual approval. Route and test selection remain with you through the UI.

options.title: Route 1: Self-contained soft glass counter
options.detail: Use CSS backdrop blur with a readable solid fallback, plus restrained transitions that respect reduced-motion preferences. Main additional risk: readability in the target browser. Effort unknown.
options.test: Offline in the target Windows browser: start at 0, click increment twice → 2, reset → 0. Repeat using Tab and Enter, then Space. Check readable controls with blur disabled and motion reduced.

options.title: Route 2: Static counter, simpler option
options.detail: Use the same counter logic and native buttons with an opaque panel and no animation. This simplifies visual verification but revises the supplied glass and motion direction. Effort unknown.
options.test: Offline in the target Windows browser: start at 0, click increment twice → 2, reset → 0. Repeat using Tab and Enter, then Space; verify visible keyboard focus.
